newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Kim orders steps to stabilise forex mart.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Kim orders steps to stabilise forex mart.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Monday ordered his economic ministers to take steps to stabilise the local foreign exchange market where the local currency has fallen sharply.
A presidential spokesman told reporters that Kim also asked the ministers to advance the opening of the local capital market to foreign investment to help promote the inflow of funds.

"The government should pursue measures to stabilise the foreign exchange market which faces difficulties due to the expansion of a current account deficit," the spokesman quoted Kim as telling a meeting with economic ministers.
Kim said the South Korean economy's credibility had been damaged by the collapses this year of Hanbo Steel Co and Sammi Steel Co.
He said policymakers must make sure companies, particularly small and medium-sized firms, would not be hit by a credit crunch.
"Measures must be taken to prevent the collapse of sound enterprises due to a temporary fund shortage," Kim said.
Kim said the liberalisation of the capital market would also help local firms raise funds in overseas financial markets.

Finance minister Kang Kyong-shik said in the meeting the ministry would let state banks expand overseas borrowings in the near future to end a shortage of dollars caused by South Korea's current account deficit.
The shortfall rose to $2.45 billion in February from $1.97 billion a year before.
Kim's remarks helped the won, which had fallen about six percent against the dollar since the start of 1997, to gain value to 884.00 in Monday afternoon from 897.50 on Friday.
